evidence.quote: The 2 left-sided renal arteries were incorporated using BIS2T. First, a 5×39 mm VBX stent-graft was deployed from the directional branch to the inferiorly located left renal artery, with distal extension using a 5×30 mm self-expanding Pulsar stent-graft (Biotronik, Lake Oswego, Oregon). An Outback Elite reentry device (Cordis) was used for creation of an in situ fenestration in the VBX stent-graft segment. A 0.014″ PT2 guidewire (Boston Scientific, Minneapolis, Minnesota) was advanced into the second superiorly located left renal artery, followed by predilatation of the in situ fenestration with a 3 mm NC Trek balloon (Abbott Cardiovascular). After guidewire exchange, a PK Papyrus (Biotronik; Lake Oswego) 3.5×23 mm balloon-expandable stent-graft was deployed into the renal artery. Then, a third stent-graft (PK Papyrus 4.5×26 mm) was deployed inside the VBX in the BIS2T overlapping segment. Final angiography demonstrated patent bifurcated stent-graft with no endoleak, dissection or embolization. The patient had no postoperative complications. Clinical and imaging follow-up at 6 months revealed patent stent-grafts with no evidence of endoleak, aneurysm sac expansion or stent-graft integrity issues (Figure 6).

summary.text: A 70-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, morbid obesity and cigarette-smoking history developed increasing mid-abdominal pain for several days with a large tender/pulsatile abdominal mass. CTA showed a symptomatic 6.1 cm Extent IV thoracoabdominal aneurysm involving celiac, SMA, right renal and two left renal arteries (4.5/4 mm). Chronic right common iliac occlusion had collateral reconstitution without claudication. Under general anesthesia, left femoral/axillary access and systemic heparinization, multibranch endovascular repair incorporated mesenteric/right renal targets and preserved both left renal arteries using BIS2T. Completion angiography showed patent stents and adequate renal flow without endoleak, dissection or embolization. Recovery had no reported complications; six-month clinical/imaging follow-up showed patency without endoleak, sac expansion or integrity issues. summary.text: A 78-year-old man with hypertension, cigarette-smoking history and ischemic cardiomyopathy without active symptoms had a 3.7 cm infrarenal aortic aneurysm, bilateral 3 cm common iliac aneurysms, and 4.9 cm right/4.1 cm left internal iliac aneurysms. Bilateral anterior/posterior division branches were patent, measuring 4/8 mm. Endovascular repair was recommended with E-tegra/bilateral E-iliac devices. caption_evidence.quote: Artistic illustration depicting the steps of the bifurcated in-stent in situ technique (BIS2T). A: After successful cannulation of the lower renal artery, the first balloon-expandable stent-graft with a doubled PTFE layer and sandwiched open-cell stent structure is deployed, establishing a stable connection to the directional branch. The directional branch is intentionally positioned higher than usual to allow for optimal graft alignment and future deployment of the secondary stent-grafts into the accessory renal artery. B: The in-stent in situ fenestration is created 2 cm distal to the edge of the directional branch using the Outback Elite reentry catheter (Cordis, Santa Clara, California). C: After the exchange of the reentry catheter for a 3 mm angioplasty balloon, the in situ fenestration is predilated to prepare for catheterization of the accessory renal artery. D: Following the successful selective catheterization of the second target vessel, the second balloon-expandable bridging stent is deployed. E: Finally, the “buddy” system is used, with a 0.018 inch angioplasty balloon positioned in the BIS2T overlapping area through the accessory renal artery. A third balloon-expandable stent is deployed into the main renal artery in a kissing balloon technique to achieve a double “D-shaped” conformation. The final configuration is confirmed by noncontrast CBCT and angiography prior to the removal of the guidewires, ensuring the desired graft shape and function.

Attached to it are plastic hoses of varying diameters: a 30 mm diameter plastic hose cranially, representing the distal thoracic aorta into which the main body of the branched stent-graft device is deployed. This phantom model is used for the technical assessment of the procedure, ensuring proper deployment and stability of the stent-graft system in different vessel sizes.
